Marissa / team —

We completed the baseline passes on 3/2–3/3. Summary of the key results below (full logs + traces attached: benchmark_results_a100_h100_l40s_v1.pdf; trace_samples_10k.jsonl). Tests used ACME canonical prompt set (mixed lengths; average generated tokens per request ~120). All tests were warm (KV cache primed), except we included a short cold-start sweep (first-token including model load) for reference.

Summary table (selected values):
- 70B FP16 (warm):
  - A100 (full): p50=38ms TTFT, p95=170ms, p99=260ms. Throughput per GPU: 70B @ concurrency 1 = 950 tokens/sec; @8 = 6,200 tokens/sec (aggregate across requests); @32 observed queuing, 95th latency jumped to ~450ms.
  - H100 (full): p50=32ms TTFT, p95=140ms, p99=220ms. Throughput: @1=1,100 tps; @8=7,500 tps; @32=27% better than A100 before queuing effects.
  - L40S (full): p50=35ms TTFT, p95=160ms, p99=240ms. Throughput: @1=1,020 tps; @8=6,600 tps. Memory headroom higher on L40S for larger KV cache.

- 70B quant-8 (warm):
  - A100 (full): p95=190ms (quality regression: +2.1% per ACME eval)
  - H100 (full): p95=160ms (quality reg: +1.9%)
  - L40S (full): p95=175ms (quality reg: +2.3%)
  -> Quantization is viable for ACME with our current eval thresholds (<=3% regression) across devices.

- 13B FP16 (warm):
  - A100 (MIG 4g equivalent partition): p50=18ms, p95=65ms, throughput @32 steady at ~12k tps across partitions.
  - L40S (MIG-equivalent): similar p95 (~68ms) with slightly better memory for cache.

MIG vs full GPU notes: 
- MIG partitions (4g/2g) provide strong density for 13B traffic — they increase aggregate throughput per physical card for small-model steady-state workloads by ~2.4x compared to single full-GPU low-concurrency jobs.
- For 70B and latency-sensitive workloads, full-GPU delivers lower p95 and much better headroom; MIG introduces jitter and higher p99s under bursty load.

Cold-start TTFT: including model load (cold container spin-up) added ~450–650ms for first token on all hardware; we recommend warm pools for production SLOs.

Stability: 30-minute sustained runs at target loads showed <2% variance in p95 on H100, ~3–4% on L40S, ~5% on A100 under identical configs.

Recommendation (one-line):
- For ACME 70B production target (p95 <= 250ms @8 concurrency): prefer H100 full-GPU reserved pool for primary traffic; supplement with L40S for models benefiting from larger cache and cost optimization. Use A100 reserved capacity as overflow/burst if pricing favors it.
- For 13B steady-state: MIG partitions on L40S or A100 are cost-efficient and provide higher density.
- Start with: 6 H100 full cards (reserve) + 8 L40S (mixed MIG for 13B) as initial Dedicated sizing to cover forecasted Q3 volume in our sizing model (detailed numbers in attached MAP).
